name: Roy Kaufmann

bio.statement: In his voters' pamphlet statement, Kaufmann lists his occupation as communications adviser, with communications work for local and state governments, nonprofits and higher education.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Communications Adviser Occupational Background: Communications for local and state governments, nonprofits, and higher education.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas County edition), p. 45

bio.statement: Kaufmann lists a bachelor's from UC Davis and a master's from the University of San Diego.
bio.excerpt: Educational Background: Bachelor's, UC Davis; Master's, University of San Diego

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas County edition), p. 45

bio.statement: Kaufmann lists no prior governmental experience.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas County edition), p. 45

positions.statement: Kaufmann says he will fight for a single-payer health plan covering every Oregonian.
positions.excerpt: I'll fight for a single-payer health plan that covers every Oregonian

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas County edition), p. 45

positions.statement: Kaufmann says he will fight for a state bank.
positions.excerpt: I'll fight for a state bank, to keep more of our wealth here.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas County edition), p. 45

positions.statement: Kaufmann says he will keep farmland growing food instead of data centers.
positions.excerpt: I'll keep our farmlands growing food instead of data centers.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas County edition), p. 45

positions.statement: Kaufmann says he owns guns and believes people can agree on measures to reduce gun violence.
positions.excerpt: I own guns, I respect the people who do, and I’m confident we can still agree on measures that reduce gun violence.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Clackamas County edition), p. 45
